title: I answer 911 calls overnight. A caller just reported my crash. It hasn't happened yet.
transcript:
I answer 911 calls overnight. A caller just reported my crash. It hasn't happened yet. "Nine one one, what's your emergency?"

A woman, calm as a recording. "A crash on Hollow Creek Road. Silver hatchback. The driver isn't moving." Then she read me the plate. My plate.

I'm the only dispatcher on overnight. My car was out in the lot, parked under the one lamp that still works. My shift ends at six. Hollow Creek is the road I take home.

I sent a patrol car anyway. Ten minutes later, the officer radioed back. No crash. No skid marks. "Just a woman by the guardrail," he said. "She's pointing down the road… and smiling."

At five, she called again. Same voice. "He's still in his seat. He doesn't feel the cold anymore. There's a woman in the back, keeping him company."

So I decided. I wasn't driving home. Not in the dark. I'd wait for sunrise, call my brother, sleep in the break room, anything.

I pulled up the parking lot camera to check on my car.

It was still under the lamp. The dome light was on. Someone was sitting in the back seat, perfectly still, facing the building.

Then my desk phone rang. The screen showed where the call was coming from. Inside my car.

"Your shift's over," she said. "Get in."
